source.snippet: Introduce first-class retry policies for failed deployment actions, including delay/backoff behavior, status code matching rules, and support in rollouts plus auto-assignments. Goal: Improve success rates for transient failures while keeping resource usage controlled and observable. Device-side installations can fail for transient reasons (for example unstable connectivity, temporary service issues). In many cases, a retry succeeds, but today recovery is mostly manual.

problem_statement: IoT and edge device management platforms lack configurable, first-class retry and backoff policies for failed OTA deployments, forcing operations teams to manually recover from transient failures at scale—an expensive and error-prone process when managing thousands of devices.
target_segment: IoT platform engineers and DevOps teams at companies deploying OTA firmware/software updates to fleets of edge devices, using open-source or commercial device management platforms.
notes: Feature request filed against hawkbit (Eclipse Foundation IoT project), widely used in industrial and automotive IoT. The requester describes a detailed, well-scoped engineering problem with explicit business impact (manual recovery cost, transient failure rates). Professional context: this is a company engineering team, not a hobbyist. Opportunity: a managed layer on top of existing device management platforms providing configurable retry/rollback/observability policies, sold as SaaS to IoT platform operators. Buyer willingness to pay is tied directly to fleet size and failure rate cost savings.
